items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Steinbeck. >> [INTERVIEWEE] Steinbeck, yeah, the people who went there.

ctx.x: Steinbeck, yeah, the people who went there. I mean Condon’s was a great place. Then of course at the time bebop was there, and that was the other side of the fence. These were totally extremes. And even the big bands too, were another extreme. Because the Condon guys thought that if you worked in a big band, you were somewhat selling out, you know, you were sacrificing the jazz for commercial security. But of course there was so much work there, in New York particularly, back in ‘46, I mean there were so many…
